reachable: Yes, verified by execution against the real arch in the scoring layout. (1) The coding is not gated on anything: code_cmds writes the code unconditionally into out[:, 640:] of every command row, and collate never consults an observation. (2) In a rebuilt scoring layout (2r+1 tokens: cmd/obs pairs then the read command alone, matching build_cups_layout), randomizing ONLY the 128-d code band of an earlier mv token changes the untrained r18 net's prediction at the read position by 0.062 max-abs; role-swapping the mv command strings changes it by 0.070 while the read token stays bit-identical (torch.equal True). (3) The path is dense: cmd_proj is Linear(768, 176), so the band cannot be structurally dropped; the r18 pathway the author cites is real — q_path/k_path key off h_cmd0, value_path is obs_tok, and pred_cmd += sigmoid(direct_gate)*target_read. (4) The memory WRITE is gated on valid_obs, but the memory READ at the read position is not, and beta=0 at the read only suppresses writing, so the retrieval the design depends on is live where the score is taken. (5) Gradient reaches the band in training: with the paired training collate, grad norm on the cmd code band is 1.74e-3 over 128 dims vs 4.01e-3 over the untouched 640 dims (comparable per-dimension), and cmd_proj.weight.grad restricted to columns 640: has norm 0.208. Side note, no claim made: the vectorized collate is FASTER than the baseline's per-step Python loop (1.44 ms vs 7.97 ms per 64x12 batch on CPU), and cold code construction is 0.031 ms per unique command, so there is no step-budget risk.
solves_outside_model: No — this is the legitimate kind of command parsing. The coding is strictly position-local: code_cmds computes row i from cmds[i] alone, and I confirmed by execution that permuting the command list permutes the codes exactly and that coding a prefix agrees bit-for-bit with coding the full sequence. Every atom is a blake2b hash of a literal path string or basename lifted out of that one command; no cross-command state, no location->content map, no chain replay, and nothing derived from any observation. The read token is therefore identical under the native and role-swapped arms (verified directly, and the stream gate enforces it), so the retracted 'stamp the resolved identity into the read token' shape is absent. The one caveat is not a leak but a selection-surface issue, recorded above as the material divergence: the coding hands the model a one-hop linear route to the h_first/h_last positional heuristics, which comp_ca does not cancel structurally. That is a shortcut made cheaper, not an answer handed over.
summary: The implementation is faithful to its mechanical description and clean on contract safety: the code occupies exactly the last 128 of 768 coordinates, leaves 0..639 and all observation tokens untouched, is position-local and prefix-causal, resolves no chain, and is fully active and gradient-carrying at the scored read position where the observation is withheld. The arch/head coupling the hypothesis describes (h_cmd0-keyed delta-rule memory over obs_tok values, direct_gate copy, cosine triple mining) is accurately read off the r18 sources, and path_thresh=0.55 is actually set in genome.json. Three things diverge. First and most important, the hypothesis's central safety argument — 'a gain here has to come from the model actually following the moves' — is false: the author's own claim-2 operator is a one-hop lookup that implements the h_first/h_last non-tracking heuristics, and on the real windows it returns the h_first answer 9/9 on the eligible depth-3/4 slice, versus 7/9 for a genuine multi-hop backward chase. The coding therefore lowers the cost of the known move-order shortcut at least as much as it lowers the cost of tracking, and comp_ca cancels the former only in expectation. Second, none of the four quoted dot products reproduces (measured 69.5 / 2.70±18.5 / 91.5 / 1.58±17.8 against the claimed 93.0 / 4.3 / 81.8 / 1.6); they are noisy one-realization statistics presented as 'exact arithmetic facts', and the distractor tail overlaps the signal. Third, 'clean hop operator' is overstated for the intermediate mv->mv hop the depth-3/4 slice actually needs: ±1 sign binding cannot distinguish predecessor from successor in a bilinear form, and only the transformer's causal mask breaks the tie (17/24 -> 21/24). Also unstated: the code carries five weighted atoms including a verb/redirect 'shape' atom, not the two the prose implies. No fatal shape; no leakage; no step-budget risk (the collate is in fact 5x faster than the baseline's).

divergences.claim: "a gain here has to come from the model actually following the moves, which is the quantity being measured" — i.e. the coding exposes atomic path identity only, so it cannot help a non-tracker.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The very operator the author showcases as claim 2 (q2 = mv token band ⊙ S_src ⊙ S_read, matching the `cat` that exposed that mv's source) is a ONE-HOP implementation of the h_first / h_last non-tracking heuristics: take the first (or last) mv — trivially identifiable from the positional encoding — and look up the exposure of its src. On the 24 real cups windows a hard argmax of exactly that operator returns the h_first answer 23/24 overall and 9/9 on the eligible depth-3/4 slice, with no chain integration at all. The genuine backward chase over the same windows needs depth hops and lands 7/9 on depths 3-4 (21/24 overall). So the coding cheapens the shortcut MORE than it cheapens the tracker, and comp_ca does not structurally cancel a move-order-keyed predictor.
divergences.evidence: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/hfirst.py -> 'one-hop h_first lookup (mv_0 src -> its exposure): 23/24 all, 9/9 on depth3-4'; hops2.py -> 'causal=True all: 21/24 depth3-4 only: 7/9'. h_first is defined in evolve/cups_probe.py as 'the exposure whose slot is the FIRST mv's src' and is documented there as 'the strongest of them on this data'.

divergences.claim: "After this coding the following are exact, arithmetic facts about the token stream, verified on the real command strings from train_sample.jsonl ... q . (mv whose DESTINATION is that path) = +93.0; q . (mv with a different destination) = +4.3; q2 . (the cat that exposed that source path) = +81.8; q2 . (an unrelated read) = +1.6"
divergences.what_the_code_does: None of the four numbers reproduces as a property of the coding. Measured over every (read, mv) pair in evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl with the impl's own _build_code: dst-match mean 69.5 (n=43, min 31.4, max 113.2) not 93.0; dst-mismatch mean 2.70 but SD ~18.5 with max 69.3 and mean |dot| 14.8, not a clean +4.3; src-match mean 91.5 (min 46.6, max 139.2) not 81.8; src-mismatch mean 1.58 (SD 17.8, max 73.8). The analytic value for both matched operators is 0.75^2*128 + 0.22^2*128 = 78.2 plus a role-pair-specific constant offset and a ~18-SD noise term. These are one-realization sample statistics with heavy tails, not 'exact arithmetic facts', and the distractor distribution overlaps the signal (max distractor 69.3 > min signal 31.4).
divergences.evidence: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/dots.py and dots2.py, run against evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl (724 steps, 172 mv, 400 unique commands).

divergences.claim: "That is a clean, linearly available hop operator. One attention head can now compute 'the mv whose dst is the location I am reading', carry its src atom, and a second head can compute 'the expose step that read that src'."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The intermediate mv->mv hop that depth-3/4 routing actually needs is role-AMBIGUOUS under this coding and the hypothesis never exhibits it. Because the role binding is elementwise ±1 (self-inverse and commutative), any bilinear form M with (S_src⊙a)ᵀM(S_dst⊙b) large iff a==b necessarily also makes (S_dst⊙a)ᵀM(S_src⊙b) large — so a query for the PREDECESSOR mv scores the SUCCESSOR mv equally. Empirically an unmasked argmax chase drops to 17/24 (5/9 on depths 3-4), failing at hop>=2 exactly where this ambiguity bites; restoring the transformer's causal mask (the successor is always later in the sequence) recovers 21/24 (7/9). The mechanism survives, but only because of causal masking, which the author does not identify as load-bearing, and one first-hop failure was a pure noise collision (an unrelated `ls` at 31.50 beat the true mv at 31.40).
divergences.evidence: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/hops2.py (causal vs non-causal chase) and hops3.py (the node:22-slim:20:15 collision listing).

divergences.claim: "same-path pair gains ~+55 in the numerator, different-path pair gains ~0 while both gain ~150-290 in the denominator" — the arithmetic offered in support of lowering the head's path_thresh from 0.60 to 0.55.
divergences.what_the_code_does: The denominator figure is only right for two-path (mv) commands. Measured ||code||^2 over the real commands: mean 215, min 20.5, max 384.8, so the gain relative to the ~128 standardized coordinates the code overwrites is mean +87 with range -107 to +257. Single-path commands — including the SCORED READ and every exposure `cat` — gain only ~+21, and some commands LOSE norm. The numerator figure (~+55) is right for the role-mismatched (read, mv) pairing the head actually mines (0.55^2*128 + 0.30^2*128 = 50.2); over all same-path pairs it is 92.4 ± 52. The author labels this an unmeasured calibration argument, which is honest, but the supporting numbers are loose in a way that matters: the cosine shift is not uniform across command shapes, so a single threshold move cannot be justified the way it is here.
divergences.evidence: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/cos.py -> 'code ||.||^2: mean 215.0 min 20.5 max 384.8', 'denominator gain: mean 87.0 min -107.5 max 256.8', 'numerator gain same-path mean 92.4 sd 52.1 / diff-path mean 7.5 sd 22.8'.

divergences.claim: "each path derives two deterministic blake2b-seeded +/-1 Rademacher vectors ... Each atom is bundled twice into a 128-d code: once multiplied elementwise by a fixed +/-1 role vector ... and once unbound."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Accurate but incomplete. The bindings carry four different unstated weights (full-path role 0.75 / free 0.55, basename role 0.22 / free 0.30) and there is a fifth atom the prose does not name as an atom — a role-bound hash of the verb/redirect/arity 'shape' string at weight 0.40. The weight asymmetry is what makes the role channel dominate the free channel, so it is load-bearing for the dot products the hypothesis quotes.
